Four constraints, and they pull against each other:
(a) never declare more than the node's real disk        HARD
(b) a minimum that fits a 200-300 GiB box
(c) on a bigger box, use the storage rather than idle it
(d) heterogeneous hardware, so it is a per-deployment choice
(c) CANNOT be satisfied by elasticity today, and this file does not pretend
otherwise. Growing a PVC after the fact needs `allowVolumeExpansion` plus a
filesystem grow, and SHRINKING a PVC is not supported by Kubernetes at all —
the only way down is destroy-and-restore. So a volume sized for a big box can
never be moved to a small one, which makes 'size it big and shrink later' a
one-way door. A ladder chosen ONCE at bring-up is the honest mechanism until
a resize path exists. See docs in storage-profiles.ts §WHAT THIS IS NOT.
== THE ARITHMETIC A PROFILE HAS TO SURVIVE ==============================
Longhorn does not make a node's whole disk schedulable. Two settings bound it,
both left at chart defaults by applications/longhorn/Application.yaml:
storageMinimalAvailablePercentage   default 25   (longhorn-1.7.2/values.yaml
line ~216: 'The default
value is 25')
storageOverProvisioningPercentage   default 100  (same file, line ~214)
so schedulable ~= 0.75 x (disk - OS root). A profile total T therefore needs a
box of roughly  T / 0.75 + ~30 GiB of root  before Longhorn will place it:
minimal    200 GiB declared  ->  ~267 GiB Longhorn disk  ->  a ~300 GiB box
standard   595 GiB declared  ->  ~793 GiB Longhorn disk  ->  a ~850 GiB box
measured   967 GiB declared  ->  ~1289 GiB Longhorn disk ->  see below
large     1599 GiB declared  ->  ~2132 GiB Longhorn disk ->  a ~2.2 TiB box
`measured` is the rung this deployment runs, and the row above is the
misleading way to read it, which is why the auditor prints two numbers per
rung and not one. Applying T/0.75 to a DECLARED total prices in capacity
that no fresh sync provisions. `measured` provisions 467 GiB at bring-up,
so it stands up on a ~653 GiB box; the ~1289 figure is what it would need
if every Application in this catalogue were synced, which includes 500 GiB
of model-cache ceiling that nothing applies today. Both are true, neither
is a discount on the other, and both are printed.
HONEST LIMIT, stated because a profile that quietly does not fit is worse than
a red gate: `minimal` fits a 300 GiB box, NOT a 200 GiB one. A 200 GiB disk
has only ~127 GiB schedulable after the same arithmetic. The auditor does this
sum against MEASURED node capacity, so nobody has to trust this paragraph.
The active profile is NOT set here. It is `activeStorageProfile` in
full-ai-cluster/k8s/single-node-budget.json, beside nodeCount and the
acknowledgements, because it is a property of THIS deployment and the ledger
is already the deployment's checked-in record. This file is the catalogue.
== POD COUNTS ARE PART OF THE FOOTPRINT, AND ONE OF THEM IS A TRAP =======
A claim's cost is size x POD COUNT, and the pod count is not always in the
manifest. Each row therefore records `podsSource`:
manifest       a scalar in this repo governs it; `podsField` names it, and
the auditor cross-checks the manifest against `pods` here.
chart-default  the upstream chart decides. `podsEvidence` must cite chart,
version and the values path. The auditor CANNOT derive these
by reading our YAML, so this file is the only place they are
written down.
singleton      the component runs exactly one pod by construction.
MEASURED 2026-08-21, and this is why the field exists: the readiness auditor's
own extractor derived mimir at 150 GiB. mimir-distributed 5.5.1 ships
`ingester.replicas: 3` and `ingester.zoneAwareReplication.enabled: true` over
three zones, and templates/_helpers.tpl line 568 computes
`replicaPerZone = ceil(replicas / zones)` — so ingester renders 1 pod in each
of 3 zone StatefulSets = 3 PVCs, and store_gateway (replicas: 1, also
zone-aware) renders ceil(1/3) = 1 per zone = 3 PVCs too. Real mimir footprint
is 350 GiB, not 150. A 200 GiB under-count, in the direction that fills a disk.
The opposite error was there too: the extractor's nearest-enclosing-replicas
heuristic gave redis MASTER the `replica.replicaCount: 2` next door, counting
10 GiB that does not exist (bitnami redis `architecture: replication` runs
exactly one master). +200 and -10 against a derived 1409 is how 1599 is the
true total.
== A NUMBER WITHOUT ITS GOVERNOR IS NOT A SIZE ==========================
`prometheus: 100Gi` means nothing without a retention bound beside it. Cut
the volume, leave the governor where it was, and you have not made the
footprint smaller — you have made an eviction loop. So a row may declare
`governors`: non-capacity scalars, per profile, written and verified in the
SAME --apply pass as the size they bound. They cannot land in separate
commits and they cannot drift, because verifyProfileApplied checks them
exactly like sizes. `governorEvidence` is required and non-empty, for the
same reason `podsEvidence` is: a bound with no stated origin is a number
somebody picked and nothing can tell that from a requirement.
The one row that has governors today is prometheus. Its old `consequence`
asked whoever selected a smaller rung to remember to cut retention by hand.
An instruction to remember is the vacuity class — it reads like a guard and
constrains nothing — and replacing it with a mechanism is what this field
is for.
AN EMPTY `governors` IS A REAL ANSWER, not an omission, and the rows say
which case they are in:
moves by itself   nats. Chart 1.2.7 emits `max_file_store: {{ pvc.size }}`
when fileStore.maxSize is unset (files/config/
jetstream.yaml:17), so the server limit tracks the PVC.
no history to     mimir ingester / store-gateway / compactor. Working
govern            space; the blocks live in object storage.
no mechanism      weaviate, cockroachdb, hindsight postgres, agent-memory.
exists            They refuse writes when full. There is no scalar to turn
and the row says so instead of implying one.
DOES NOT move,    tempo. The chart default `tempo.retention: 24h`
and is left       (values.yaml:57 -> compactor block_retention) is a TIME
window that cannot see the disk, so shrinking the volume
does not shorten it. Cutting it would need a measured

The residual risk is named in the manifest instead.
== SCHEDULED AT BRING-UP vs DECLARED ====================================
`scheduledAtBringUp: false` means no PVC object is created on a fresh sync, so
the capacity is planning-only. It is NOT a discount on the hard constraint:
the moment a maintainer syncs the app, the full size lands. Longhorn's
StorageClass is `volumeBindingMode: Immediate` (hardcoded at
longhorn-1.7.2/templates/storageclass.yaml line 18, not configurable), so an
applied PVC provisions its replica with ZERO consuming pods — `replicas: 0` on
the workload buys nothing. What buys it is the Application never being applied.
So the auditor convicts on DECLARED and merely REPORTS bring-up. A gate that
convicted on the bring-up subset would pass today and fail the first time
someone ran `argocd app sync ollama`, which is a check that did not run
wearing the face of one that passed.

== A REQUEST IS A RESERVATION, NOT A MEASUREMENT ========================
Cutting a request below the app's real working set does not make the app smaller.
Without a matching limit it makes the pod more over-committed, and moves the
failure from a Pending pod (loud, scheduler-attributed) to the kernel OOM killer
(quiet, arbitrary). So every row that cuts has to say what the cut costs, and the
loader refuses one that does not.
AND THE SUM IS A FLOOR, NOT THE REQUIREMENT. 28 of the 45 Applications render
pods that request NOTHING (`resources: {}` chart defaults). Those pods are
BestEffort: the scheduler admits any number of them and no arithmetic here ever
sees them. The envelope's unreserved headroom is what they actually run in.

== THE CLAIM THIS BLOCK USED TO MAKE, AND WHY IT IS WITHDRAWN ============
WRITTEN 2026-08-23 against a tree where this floor was the ONLY thing standing
between 3 lanes and 2. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-23 after rebasing onto #14174 and
#14194, and THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE. The correction is recorded rather than
overwritten, because a claim that was right about one tree and wrong about this
one is exactly the kind of thing that silently outlives its arithmetic.
Measured on THIS tree, `lane-partition.ts --rung dev`, margin 0.85, envelope 70:
floor        lanes   covered   busiest lane CPU   of 2125m budget
THE LANE COUNT DOES NOT MOVE AT ANY FLOOR. 3 lanes became 2, and 41/47 became
43/47, because of TWO OTHER CHANGES: the maintainer's `freeDiskGib` 14 -> 70
(see `measuredFreeDiskEvidence`), which un-quarantined `hindsight` and `vllm`,
and #14194 making raw in-repo manifests rung-reachable, which took all-47 dev
CPU 6166m -> 5191m and gmod 1000m -> 100m at this rung. EVERY ROW OF THE TABLE
HOLDS `game-hosting/gmod` AT 100m, including the OFF row: it is left at the
value #14194 chose for it and is deliberately NOT floored here, because
extending this floor to a row governed after the floor was authorized would be
extending an authorization rather than inheriting one. A uniform floor that did
reach gmod would read 75m lower at 25m, and would still not change a lane.
SO WHAT THE FLOOR ACTUALLY BUYS ON THIS TREE IS HEADROOM, NOT A LANE: the
busiest lane goes from 77.9% of its CPU budget to 50.9%. That is worth having
and it is what Aaron asked for -- room to test more charts without the next
workload re-splitting the partition -- but it is a smaller claim than the one
this block was written to make, and the smaller claim is the true one.
CPU is COMPRESSIBLE and memory is not, and the two failure modes are not
comparable. An under-requested CPU pod is THROTTLED -- it runs slower, it is
never killed for it. An under-requested memory pod is OOM-KILLED, which is the
quiet, arbitrary failure this file already warns about under 'A REQUEST IS A
RESERVATION, NOT A MEASUREMENT'. So the floor touches only the axis where being
wrong is recoverable and visible.
And a request is a SCHEDULING input plus a cgroup share, not a ceiling. Nothing
here lowers a limit -- arc-controller and node-feature-discovery are the two
rows that even have one, and both keep theirs. What the cut actually spends is
GUARANTEED share under contention: a 25m pod on a busy runner gets less CPU and
starts slower, so the real risk is a readiness probe running out of slack. That
fails LOUDLY (NotReady, CrashLoop, an attributable pod) and is undone by raising
this floor. It is the trade, stated, not a claim that the cut is free.
25m is not a coinage: it is already this catalogue's value for its smaller dev
rows (mimir/ruler, mimir/query_frontend, mimir/overrides_exporter, temporal/web,
node-feature-discovery/gc and /worker all sat at 25 before this). The floor
adopts the file's own number rather than inventing one. Since no floor changes
the lane count on this tree, 25 is now chosen for the headroom / guaranteed-share
trade above and NOT because it is the value that buys the partition.
`gitlab` IS 2525m AND IS THE ONE APPLICATION STILL QUARANTINED. It has no
`resourceClaims` row at all -- it is glob-excluded from the dev lane and carried
in `ungovernedRequests` -- so this floor cannot touch it, and 2525m is over the
2125m per-lane budget on its own. Its DISK half DID clear: at the 70-GiB
envelope its 11.53Gi closure fits a 56.10Gi lane, so gitlab went from oversize
on BOTH axes to oversize on CPU alone. Governing it is a separate decision with
a separate blast radius and is not taken here.
`game-hosting/gmod` is 100m at `dev` since #14194 and 1000m at `metal`. It is
counted, not excluded; reachability is not removal.

THE DISK HALF WAS THE VENDOR SPEC (14 GB free SSD), which understated the machine by more than 5x; it is now 70 GiB, TAKEN BY THE MAINTAINER 2026-08-23 -- see `measuredFreeDiskEvidence` beside it for the verbatim authorization, the two runners it is a floor beneath, and the standing tripwire on any further change. `runner-disk.ts --check-envelope` convicts when a runner has LESS than this declares, so raising the bound STRENGTHENS that check rather than weakening it: it used to catch only a machine below 14 GiB, which is no machine this fleet runs on, and it now catches any runner that cannot hold what the lanes were planned against. The cost of the raise is stated rather than hidden: a hosted runner that ever ships with less than 70 GiB free will now FAIL this gate, and that failure is the gate working. 16 GB is recorded as 15360Mi because GB is decimal and Kubernetes quantities are binary. THE RESERVED HALF is 1500m / 6144Mi and splits three ways. (1) ~950m / ~290Mi for the kind control plane and kube-system, which the scheduler subtracts from allocatable before any Application is placed: kubeadm's static-pod defaults (apiserver 250m, controller-manager 200m, scheduler 100m, etcd 100m/100Mi), coredns 2 x 100m/70Mi, kindnet 100m/50Mi. argo-cd 7.7.10 adds nothing -- rendered 2026-08-21, every component's `resources` is unset. (2) ~550m / ~1536Mi ESTIMATED for what lives outside the kind node's cgroup and which the scheduler therefore cannot see at all: the host OS, the Actions runner agent, dockerd/containerd, and the bun harness driving the run. kind imposes no memory limit on its node container, so the kubelet reports the HOST's capacity as the node's -- meaning this slice is real and invisible, and under-reserving it shows up as the runner OOMing rather than as a Pending pod. (3) the remaining ~4300Mi is UNRESERVED HEADROOM for BestEffort pods. 28 of the 45 Applications render pods that request nothing, so the scheduler will admit any number of them and this arithmetic will never see one. That headroom is the only thing standing between them and the kernel OOM killer, and it is the reason this budget is deliberately not tight.
